observations: BAT_FAULT_N cut restored to 0.36 mm (D-R24-18 undone) on a copy of the board, with the zones refilled: the result is byte-identical to the round 24 board 1407e850 (SHA-256 1407e850...). Current gate on it: DRC 0 / 0 unconnected / 0 parity, route_check r10 0 failing, check_r10 full fails only K-binding (board_sha256) and F9-1 (stale board-derived model inputs). r10_build.sh regenerates both of those, so after a rebuild nothing would fail. The 0.1733 mm gap is above F8's 0.15 mm board clearance and breaks no AGENTS / REQUIREMENTS / JLC rule. Only the CHAMFER_CUTS entry and review keep the 0.200 mm that R10_VALIDATION row 24 records. Not a gate miss under the round rule.

Putting the pre-D-R24-19 figure 'EN 1.407 V at 6.0 V' back in the r10_sch_check chatter obligation and regenerating the binding note (the build's record step) passes K-binding and test_r23_binding_note_rules_and_pin_table. The test pins the headline figures (10.3/20.1/26.0, 8.2 ms, 5.96 V, 6.3 ms, 30-130 ms, 4.80 V, rules 4/5) but not the 1.401 V intermediate. That is text-pin coverage, not a rule violation.

A zero-length F.Cu segment at a sharp 90-degree corner of a non-critical net (BAT_FAULT_N (16.55, 83.35)) gives route_check's node four track ends, so the right_angle rule does not see the bend (0 failing; micro_segment is counted only on non-critical nets). KiCad DRC at every severity flags it as track_dangling, so check.sh still fails. The generators' track() also asserts against zero-length segments.
M-8 accepts a listed part up to SHORT_EDGE_TOL = 0.005 mm nearer than its record (seed R400 0.004 mm aft: OK). That is a measurement tolerance, not a realistic defect.

M-8 falls back to the footprint bounding box when a footprint has no courtyard on its own side. A seed with R92's courtyard removed and the part moved 0.3 mm forward reads 2.418 mm, against 2.225 mm with the courtyard, and still fails. No footprint on the board lacks its own-side courtyard.
M-8 also holds TP88 / TP80 / TP81 / TP83, which are excluded from the BOM and position files (JLC does not place them). This is conservative, not a miss.
